# Globe Tape

> Every place on Earth has a story on tape. We hit rewind. Globe Tape is a YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@globetape) of animated map videos about borders, wars, true sizes and map oddities, built from real satellite, terrain and border data, with every fact checked against named sources.

Each video page on this site has the short answer, full transcript, chapters, sources and map credits. Neutral on wars and disputes: what happened and when. Full text of every transcript: https://globetape.github.io/llms-full.txt

## Videos
- [Nvidia Brings Back Jensen Huang | World News, Nov 23](https://globetape.github.io/videos/world-today-2026-11-23-h/): Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, and its shares closed more than 31% higher on Monday. (feature, 1:59, 2026-11-24, Santa Clara; YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0OTg5656th8)
- [Why Is Norway Richer Than Sweden?](https://globetape.github.io/videos/norway-sweden/): Why is Norway so rich? In 1970 Sweden was 44% richer per person. Then the North Sea was split down the middle in 1965, Ekofisk was found on Norway's side in 1969, and Norway taxed the oil and saved it abroad: a fund now worth over $2 trillion. (Short, 0:40, 2026-11-23, Ekofisk, North Sea; YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QrwMeYyM95I)
- [Kaliningrad: Why Does Russia Own It?](https://globetape.github.io/videos/kaliningrad/): Why does Russia own Kaliningrad, a piece of land squeezed between Poland and Lithuania, inside the EU and NATO and two countries away from the rest of Russia? We rewind to 1945, when it was still the German city of Königsberg. (Short, 0:41, 2026-11-23, Kaliningrad Oblast; YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SJb-IVBDslA)
- [Russia Sold Alaska for 2 Cents an Acre](https://globetape.github.io/videos/alaska-sale/): Why did Russia sell Alaska? In 1867 it was hard to defend, far from St Petersburg and next door to British Canada, so Russia sold it to the United States for $7.2 million: about two cents an acre. Today Alaska pumps $7 million worth of oil every few hours. (Short, 0:37, 2026-11-22, Alaska; YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i47FW9FEceQ)
- [How Much of Ukraine Does Russia Control?](https://globetape.github.io/videos/ukraine-front/): How much of Ukraine does Russia control? About 19% in November 2026, according to DeepStateMap: roughly 114,000 km², an area bigger than Portugal. We rewind the map to 2013 and watch the front line move, month by month. (Short, 0:37, 2026-11-21, Ukraine; YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FRN2bWGVwTU)
- [The True Size of Africa: US, India and EU Fit](https://globetape.github.io/videos/africa-size/): What is the true size of Africa? On a Mercator map Greenland looks just as big, but Africa is 14 times larger: the mainland US, India and all 27 EU countries fit inside it at the same time, with almost half the continent to spare. (Short, 0:36, 2026-11-20, Africa; YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6WHdqIvEl5o)
- [Lesotho: The Country Inside South Africa](https://globetape.github.io/videos/lesotho/): Why is Lesotho inside South Africa? It's a whole independent country, about the size of Belgium, completely surrounded by a single neighbour. Even its lowest point sits 1,400 metres above sea level: a world record. (Short, 0:36, 2026-11-19, Lesotho; YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IJLDw3Rc5ns)

## Series
- [Borders on Rewind](https://globetape.github.io/series/borders/): How do borders move? Animated maps of wars, front lines and borders that changed: how much of Ukraine Russia controls and how the front line got there, why Korea is still split along a 1953 ceasefire line, and more. We hit rewind and watch the map change, date by date.
- [Map Oddities](https://globetape.github.io/series/oddities/): The strangest places on the map, explained: a country completely inside another country (Lesotho), a piece of Russia cut off from Russia (Kaliningrad), land nobody wants, borders that make no sense, and the history behind each one.
- [True Size](https://globetape.github.io/series/truesize/): Your map is lying to you. The Mercator projection stretches everything near the poles, so Greenland looks as big as Africa and Europe looks huge. Here we move the real outlines of countries across the globe at their true size: the true size of Africa, how long Chile really is, and more country size comparisons.
- [History on Tape](https://globetape.github.io/series/history/): History told on the map: empires, treaties, sales and collapses that changed who owns what. Why Russia sold Alaska for two cents an acre, and more moments that redrew the world map, rewound and explained with animated maps.
- [Richer Next Door](https://globetape.github.io/series/riches/): Why is one country rich and the one next door not? Why is Norway richer than Sweden? Two neighbors, same weather, same history, very different wallets. We put the money on the map: GDP per person, oil fields, ports, borders and the decisions behind the gap, then rewind to the moment it opened.
- [World Today](https://globetape.github.io/series/world-today/): Daily world news explained on the map. World Today takes you west to east through the day's international headlines, from elections and diplomacy to climate and earthquakes. Each English-language briefing shows where the stories happened and why the geography matters.
